newsitem.title: USA: Chicago Sun-Times plans $100 mln plant.
newsitem.headline: Chicago Sun-Times plans $100 mln plant.

text.p: The Chicago Sun-Times said Thursday it plans to build a $100 million printing plant and will buy six web offset presses from Goss Graphic Systems Inc for the facility which is expected to be operating by the end of 1999.
The site is under review, a company spokeswoman said.
Replacing the Sun-Times aging presses has been a top priority of the newspaper's managment since the newspaper was acquired by Hollinger International Inc in 1994, the company said.
"This is a commitment to the future of the Sun-Times and to this city, but it's also a commitment to the newspaper business," said F. David Radler, publisher, in a statement.
The new presses will print 75,000 copies of the paper per hour compared with 50,000 copies per hour on the current presses.
Hollinger International owns or has an interest in 163 daily Englilsh-language newspapers and 441 non-daily papers and magazines in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom and Israel.
